SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS 
UNIVERSITY AND SCHOOLS 


August 22nd, 1963 
NEWS RELEASE 


In the academic year of 1963-6) Sir George Williams University 
will offer, in its Evening Division, a section of several of 
its basic first-year degree courses in thé French language. This 
experimental effort is designed to be helpful to evening students 
whose first language is French and to English speaking students 

4 who are able to take university work in the French language. It 
is hoped that this opportunity will ease the problems of French 
speaking students who must work in the daytime and are embarking 
on an evening degree programme in an English language university 
and that it will also enable English speaking students to im- 


prove in bilingual abilities. 


French text books will be used, as far as possible, and copies 
of relevant books in the French language will be added to the 
library collection. It is expected that students will be per- 


mitted to write final examinations in either French or English 
and that this option will be extended, where possible, to include 


required reading and other class assignments. 


The sections of courses fo be given in the French language during 

the 1963-6), academic year are all taken from the first year re- 
quired courses which may lead to Bachelors' degrees in Arts, 

Science, Commerce, and Engineering. The French section of the 
introductory course in chemistry - "Chemistry 211, General Chemistry" 
- will be taught by Dr. R.H.C. Verschingel. Professor Hubert Guindon, 


Conti awed! 2H oteisscs 


another member of the full-time teaching faculty, wil be pre- 
senting the section in French of "Sociology 2ll, Introductory 
Sociology." "Economics 211, Introduction to Economics" will be 
taught by Mr. Stefan Lamed. The other basic courses which wil! 
offer sections in French are "Mathematics 213, Algebra," and 
"Mathematics 223, Analytical Trigonometry and Geometry." In- 
structors for these French sections are to be announced at an 
early date. At registration time, which commences on August 26th, 
French and English speaking first year students, in the Evening 
Division, will have the opportunity to indicate if they wish to 


take these courses in the French or English languages. 


Sir George Williams University is proud to serve al! members of 


the Montreal community and its student body has had broad repre- 


sentation of all language, racial and religious groupings. Ef- 

forts have always been made to aid students whose first language 
is other than English and special classes in the English language 
have been Srmahar oa as well as coaching and guidance in all fields. 


Sir George plans to. intensive ty study, during the coming year, 


. the possiblity of offering further opportunities in the French 


language to students. The results of the courses offered this 
year in the French language sections will have a bearing on the 


feasibility and practicality of increasing the number of courses 


offering sections in French.
